---
Hidden Markov model (HMM) analyses for the Helping Task
Code for: "Development and validation of a task for assessing help-seeker relational dynamics (2026)"
authors: Kwan T*, Shin J, Selai C, Zavlis O, Moutoussis M (* corresponding author)
---

This markdown file reproduces every HMM analysis reported in the paper and the supplement. All analyses read the same dataset file (rename and replace where needed), `HT_dataset.csv`, which holds Study 1 (`STUDY = 1`) and Study 2 (`STUDY = 2`).

== # == Analysis - Participants
== 1 == HMM fitted to Study 1 (TP + LE)
== 2 == HMM fitted to Study 1 (TP alone)
== 3 == HMM fitted to Study 2 (Online sample)
== 4 == #3's model applied to the LE participants, no re-fitting
== 5 == HMM fitted to the combined online and LE data

Participant groups:
 - TP = typical participants (Study 1, IDs `TP..`; random Helper in all three blocks). 
 - LE = lived experience with relational difficulties (Study 1, IDs `LE1`, `LE2`; CUC/CUU). 
 - Online = Study 2 participants recruited through Prolific (IDs `PRO..`; CUC/CUU)

Model:
- Effort (1-4), satisfaction (1-6) and trust (1-6) are categorical emissions. 
- Each row is the evaluation of trial *t* together with the effort chosen on trial *t*+1. 
- Transition covariates describe the outcome of trial *t*+1, which is what happens between the two states (see Figure 2 in the main paper)
- Models with 1 to 5 states are fitted from 15 random initialisations each. 
- A number of states is retained only if its best solution is reached by at least 3 of the 15 initialisations and every state holds at least 5% of trials; the retained model with the lowest BIC is selected. 
- States are numbered from lowest to highest expected trust.

# Setup
```{r setup, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(depmixS4)

data_dir <- "."
N_STARTS <- 15     # random initialisations per model
MIN_INIT <- 3      # initialisations that must reach the best solution
MIN_OCC  <- 0.05   # smallest share of trials any state may hold
K_MAX    <- 5      # largest number of states fitted
```

## Load dataset

```{r load-data}

raw <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "HT_dataset.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)

data <- raw %>%
  rename(
    pid             = PID,
    study           = STUDY,
    trial           = Trial,
    block           = Block,
    policy          = 'Helper Policy',
    effort_intended = 'Effort Intended',
    effort_actual   = 'Effort Actual',
    partner_effort  = 'Helper Effort',
    satisfaction    = 'Satisfaction Rating',
    trust           = 'Trust Rating',
    points_helper   = 'Points For Helper',
    points_seeker   = 'Points For Help-Seeker') %>%
  group_by(pid) %>%
  mutate(design = case_when(all(policy == "RANDOM")                 ~ "Random",
                            policy[block == 3][1] == "CARING"       ~ "CUC",
                            TRUE                                    ~ "CUU")) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(group = case_when(study == 2          ~ "Online",
                           design == "Random"  ~ "TP",
                           TRUE                ~ "LE")) %>%
  arrange(pid, block, trial)

data %>% distinct(pid, study, group, design) %>% count(study, group, design)
```

# Prep Data

```{r functions-data}
cov_cols <- c("partner_effort_z", "payoff_diff_z", "effort_diff_z")

prepare_data <- function(dat, z_ref = NULL) {
  d <- dat %>%
    arrange(pid, block, trial) %>%
    group_by(pid, block) %>%
    mutate(block_trial         = row_number(),
           effort_selection    = lead(effort_intended),
           next_partner_effort = lead(partner_effort),
           next_effort_actual  = lead(effort_actual),
           next_points_seeker  = lead(points_seeker),
           next_points_helper  = lead(points_helper),
           half = ifelse(block_trial <= n() / 2, "First half", "Second half")) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(next_payoff_diff = next_points_seeker - next_points_helper,   # + = participant came out ahead
           next_effort_diff = next_partner_effort - next_effort_actual)  # + = Helper gave more than participant

  ref <- if (is.null(z_ref)) d else z_ref
  z   <- function(var) (d[[var]] - mean(ref[[var]], na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(ref[[var]], na.rm = TRUE)

  d <- d %>% mutate(
    partner_effort_z = z("next_partner_effort"),
    payoff_diff_z    = z("next_payoff_diff"),
    effort_diff_z    = z("next_effort_diff"),
    effort_f = factor(effort_selection, levels = 1:4),   # responses as categories
    sat_f    = factor(satisfaction,     levels = 1:6),
    trust_f  = factor(trust,            levels = 1:6),
    policy_lab = case_when(policy == "CARING"   ~ "Caring",
                           policy == "UNCARING" ~ "Uncaring",
                           TRUE                 ~ "Random"))
  for (cc in cov_cols) d[[cc]][is.na(d[[cc]])] <- 0


  tp_ids <- sort(unique(d$pid[d$group == "TP"]))
  d$pid_label <- ifelse(d$group == "TP", sprintf("P%02d", match(d$pid, tp_ids)), d$pid)

  attr(d, "ntimes") <- d %>% count(pid, block) %>% pull(n)   # one sequence per participant x block
  cat("Participants:", n_distinct(d$pid), " Blocks:", length(attr(d, "ntimes")),
      " Rows:", nrow(d), "\n")
  d
}
```

# Setup HMM Model Fitting

```{r functions-model}
build_hmm <- function(d, k, trans_formula = ~ 1) {
  depmix(list(effort_f ~ 1, sat_f ~ 1, trust_f ~ 1), data = d,
         nstates = k, ntimes = attr(d, "ntimes"), transition = trans_formula,
         family = list(multinomial("identity"), multinomial("identity"),
                       multinomial("identity")))
}

fit_hmm <- function(d, k, trans_formula = ~ 1, n_starts = N_STARTS, seed_base = 1000) {
  best <- NULL; lls <- c()
  for (s in seq_len(n_starts)) {
    set.seed(seed_base + s)
    f <- NULL
    invisible(capture.output(      # hides depmixS4's "converged at iteration ..." messages
      f <- tryCatch(suppressWarnings(fit(build_hmm(d, k, trans_formula), verbose = FALSE,
             emcontrol = em.control(maxit = 1000, random.start = TRUE))),
             error = function(e) NULL)))
    if (is.null(f)) next
    lls <- c(lls, as.numeric(logLik(f)))
    if (is.null(best) || as.numeric(logLik(f)) > as.numeric(logLik(best))) best <- f
  }
  ## initialisations that reached the best solution (within 0.1 log-likelihood)
  list(fit = best, n_at_best = sum(lls > max(lls) - 0.1))
}

## depmixS4's BIC() drops rows with a missing response (the last row of every
## block). Every row is counted here instead.
ll_of  <- function(f) as.numeric(suppressWarnings(logLik(f)))
npar   <- function(f) attr(suppressWarnings(logLik(f)), "df")
bic_of <- function(f, n) -2 * ll_of(f) + log(n) * npar(f)

## Most likely state sequence (Viterbi). depmixS4's posterior(type = "viterbi")
## reads the transition covariate from the row after each move, while fitting
## reads it from the row before. This version uses the same row as fitting.
## Without covariates the two give identical results.
viterbi_fixed <- function(f, ntimes) {
  dens <- f@dens
  dens[is.na(dens)] <- 1                        # a missing response carries no information
  B <- apply(dens, c(1, 3), prod)               # P(responses | state) for every row
  A <- f@trDens                                 # A[row, to, from]
  ends <- cumsum(ntimes); starts <- ends - ntimes + 1
  state <- integer(nrow(B))
  for (s in seq_along(ntimes)) {
    rows <- starts[s]:ends[s]; n <- length(rows); k <- ncol(B)
    delta <- matrix(-Inf, n, k); back <- matrix(0L, n, k)
    delta[1, ] <- log(f@init[s, ]) + log(B[rows[1], ])
    for (t in 2:n) {
      a <- if (dim(A)[1] == 1) 1 else rows[t - 1]
      for (j in 1:k) {
        cand <- delta[t - 1, ] + log(A[a, j, ])
        back[t, j]  <- which.max(cand)
        delta[t, j] <- max(cand) + log(B[rows[t], j])
      }
    }
    path <- integer(n); path[n] <- which.max(delta[n, ])
    for (t in (n - 1):1) path[t] <- back[t + 1, path[t + 1]]
    state[rows] <- path
  }
  state
}

## P(next state | state i) for given covariate values
trans_probs <- function(f, i, newdata) {
  tm <- f@transition[[i]]
  B  <- tm@parameters$coefficients
  if (tm@family$link == "identity")
    return(matrix(as.numeric(B), nrow = NROW(newdata), ncol = length(B), byrow = TRUE))
  X   <- model.matrix(delete.response(terms(tm@formula)), newdata)
  eta <- X %*% as.matrix(B)
  exp(eta) / rowSums(exp(eta))
}

## Transition covariates compared (all describe the next trial)
specs <- list(
  "Null (no covariate)" = ~ 1,
  "Helper's effort"     = ~ partner_effort_z,   # what the Helper did
  "Payoff difference"   = ~ payoff_diff_z,      # own points - Helper's points
  "Effort difference"   = ~ effort_diff_z)      # Helper's effort - own actual effort

run_hmm <- function(d) {
  n <- nrow(d)

  ## 1. Number of states
  selection <- data.frame()
  for (k in 1:K_MAX) {
    r   <- fit_hmm(d, k, seed_base = 1000 * k)
    occ <- colMeans(posterior(r$fit, type = "smoothing"))
    selection <- rbind(selection, data.frame(
      k = k, logLik = round(ll_of(r$fit), 1), npar = npar(r$fit), BIC = round(bic_of(r$fit, n), 1),
      inits_at_best = r$n_at_best, smallest_state = round(min(occ), 3)))
  }
  selection$retained <- selection$inits_at_best >= MIN_INIT & selection$smallest_state >= MIN_OCC
  best_k <- with(selection[selection$retained, ], k[which.min(BIC)])
  cat("\nNumber of states:\n"); print(selection)
  cat("Selected k =", best_k, "\n")

  ## 2. Transition covariates
  fits <- list()
  for (j in seq_along(specs))
    fits[[names(specs)[j]]] <- fit_hmm(d, best_k, specs[[j]], n_starts = ifelse(j == 1, N_STARTS, 10),
                                       seed_base = 50000 + 1000 * j)$fit
  null <- "Null (no covariate)"
  comp <- tibble(model  = names(fits),
                 logLik = sapply(fits, ll_of),
                 npar   = sapply(fits, npar),
                 BIC    = sapply(fits, bic_of, n = n)) %>%
    mutate(dBIC = BIC - BIC[model == null],
           LR   = 2 * (logLik - logLik[model == null]),
           df   = npar - npar[model == null],
           p    = ifelse(df > 0, pchisq(LR, df, lower.tail = FALSE), NA)) %>%
    arrange(BIC)
  winner_name <- comp$model[1]                  # lowest BIC (can be the null)
  winner      <- fits[[winner_name]]
  cat("\nTransition covariates:\n"); print(comp, width = Inf)
  cat("Winning model:", winner_name, "\n")

  ## 3. Winning model: states ordered from lowest to highest expected trust
  state_labels <- paste("State", 1:best_k)
  emis_mean <- function(i, r) { p <- getpars(winner@response[[i]][[r]]); sum(seq_along(p) * p) }
  ord <- order(sapply(1:best_k, emis_mean, r = 3))

  d$state <- factor(state_labels[match(viterbi_fixed(winner, attr(d, "ntimes")), ord)],
                    levels = state_labels)
  post <- posterior(winner, type = "smoothing")[, ord]
  colnames(post) <- paste0("p_", state_labels)
  d <- bind_cols(d, as.data.frame(post))
  cat("\nMean certainty of the decoded state:", round(mean(apply(post, 1, max)), 3), "\n")

  channels <- c("Effort", "Satisfaction", "Trust")
  emis <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:best_k, function(i) do.call(rbind, lapply(1:3, function(r) {
    p <- getpars(winner@response[[ord[i]]][[r]])
    data.frame(state = state_labels[i], channel = channels[r], value = seq_along(p), prob = as.numeric(p))
  }))))
  emis$state <- factor(emis$state, levels = state_labels)
  profile <- emis %>% group_by(state, channel) %>%
    summarise(mean = sum(value * prob), .groups = "drop") %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = channel, values_from = mean)
  cat("\nState profiles (model expected values):\n"); print(as.data.frame(profile), digits = 3)

  avg <- d[1, ]; for (v in cov_cols) avg[[v]] <- 0   # average covariate values
  trans_mat <- t(sapply(1:best_k, function(i) trans_probs(winner, ord[i], avg)[1, ord]))
  dimnames(trans_mat) <- list(from = state_labels, to = state_labels)
  cat("\nTransition matrix (average covariate values):\n"); print(round(trans_mat, 3))

  list(data = d, selection = selection, best_k = best_k, fits = fits, comp = comp,
       winner = winner, winner_name = winner_name, state_labels = state_labels, ord = ord,
       emis = emis, profile = profile, trans_mat = trans_mat)
}

## Per-participant occupancy (% of trials in each decoded state), written to CSV
write_occupancy <- function(res, file) {
  occ <- res$data %>% count(pid, pid_label, group, design, state, .drop = FALSE) %>%
    group_by(pid) %>% mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) %>% ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::select(pid, pid_label, group, design, state, pct) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = state, values_from = pct, values_fill = 0)
  write.csv(occ, file.path(data_dir, file), row.names = FALSE)
  invisible(occ)
}

## Mean smoothed state probabilities by any grouping
occupancy_by <- function(res, ...) {
  res$data %>% group_by(...) %>%
    summarise(rows = n(), across(starts_with("p_"), mean), .groups = "drop") %>%
    as.data.frame()
}

## Caring vs uncaring occupancy, one value per participant (paired Wilcoxon, Holm)
policy_tests <- function(res) {
  occ <- res$data %>% filter(policy_lab != "Random") %>% group_by(pid, policy_lab) %>%
    summarise(across(starts_with("p_"), mean), .groups = "drop")
  out <- do.call(rbind, lapply(res$state_labels, function(s) {
    wide <- occ %>% dplyr::select(pid, policy_lab, occ = all_of(paste0("p_", s))) %>%
      pivot_wider(names_from = policy_lab, values_from = occ)
    w <- suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(wide$Caring, wide$Uncaring, paired = TRUE, exact = FALSE))
    data.frame(state = s, caring = mean(wide$Caring), uncaring = mean(wide$Uncaring), p = w$p.value)
  }))
  out$p_holm <- p.adjust(out$p, method = "holm")
  out
}

## Save one analysis as .RData. Stores the whole result list as `res`, plus each
## piece under the names the figure code uses, plus the helpers it needs, so the
## figures can be made in a fresh R session with just load().
save_results <- function(res, file) {
  e <- new.env()
  e$res          <- res
  e$data_adj     <- res$data
  e$seq_id       <- paste(res$data$pid, res$data$block)      # one sequence per participant x block
  e$ntimes_block <- attr(res$data, "ntimes")
  sel <- res$selection
  sel$starts_at_best <- sel$inits_at_best                    # names used in the figure code
  sel$reliable       <- sel$retained
  e$selection    <- sel
  for (nm in c("best_k", "fits", "comp", "winner", "winner_name", "state_labels",
               "ord", "emis", "profile", "trans_mat")) assign(nm, res[[nm]], envir = e)
  e$cov_vars     <- all.vars(specs[[res$winner_name]])       # empty if the null model wins
  e$cov_cols     <- cov_cols
  e$specs        <- specs
  e$trans_probs  <- trans_probs
  save(list = ls(e), envir = e, file = file.path(data_dir, file))
}
```

# 1. Study 1: TP + LE

```{r analysis-1}
d1   <- prepare_data(filter(data, study == 1))
res1 <- run_hmm(d1)

occupancy_by(res1, group, design, policy_lab)
write_occupancy(res1, "occupancy_1_study1.csv")
save_results(res1, "hmm_1_study1.RData")

```

# 2. Study 1: TP alone

```{r analysis-2}
d2   <- prepare_data(filter(data, study == 1, group == "TP"))
res2 <- run_hmm(d2)

write_occupancy(res2, "occupancy_2_tp.csv")
save_results(res2, "hmm_2_tp.RData")
```

# 3. Study 2: online sample

```{r analysis-3}
d3   <- prepare_data(filter(data, study == 2))
res3 <- run_hmm(d3)

occupancy_by(res3, policy_lab, half)
policy_tests(res3)
write_occupancy(res3, "occupancy_3_online.csv")
save_results(res3, "hmm_3_online.RData")
```

# 4. LE participants under the Study 2 model (no re-fitting)

```{r analysis-4}
if (!exists("res3")) { load(file.path(data_dir, "hmm_3_online.RData")); res3 <- res }

d4 <- prepare_data(filter(data, group == "LE"), z_ref = res3$data)

## Same structure as the Study 2 winner, with its estimates copied in (no fit()).
## Build only on data containing every response category: depmixS4 drops
## categories that never occur, which would change the parameter count.
with_fixed_pars <- function(d, res) {
  m <- build_hmm(d, res$best_k, specs[[res$winner_name]])
  p <- getpars(res$winner)
  if (length(getpars(m)) != length(p))
    stop("Parameter count differs from the fitted model: a response category is missing from these data")
  setpars(m, p)
}

## Check: re-evaluating on the Study 2 data reproduces its log-likelihood
stopifnot(abs(ll_of(with_fixed_pars(res3$data, res3)) - ll_of(res3$winner)) < 1e-3)

fb       <- forwardbackward(with_fixed_pars(d4, res3))
ll_fixed <- fb$logLike
ll_on    <- ll_of(res3$winner)
n_on     <- nrow(res3$data)
n_LE    <- nrow(d4)
ll_chance <- sum(ifelse(is.na(d4$effort_f), 0, log(1/4))) + n_LE * 2 * log(1/6)

data.frame(
  data       = c("Online (model fitted to these data)", "LE (online model, fixed)", "LE, chance"),
  rows       = c(n_on, n_LE, n_LE),
  logLik     = c(ll_on, ll_fixed, ll_chance),
  ll_per_row = c(ll_on / n_on, ll_fixed / n_LE, ll_chance / n_LE))

## Per LE participant: each row's contribution under the one fixed model
row_ll <- -log(fb$sca)
stopifnot(abs(sum(row_ll) - ll_fixed) < 1e-4)
d4 %>% mutate(row_ll = row_ll) %>% group_by(pid, design) %>%
  summarise(rows = n(), logLik = sum(row_ll), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(ll_per_row = logLik / rows) %>% as.data.frame()
```

# 5. Combined online and LE data

```{r analysis-5}
d5   <- prepare_data(filter(data, group %in% c("Online", "LE")))
res5 <- run_hmm(d5)

occupancy_by(res5, policy_lab, half)
policy_tests(res5)
write_occupancy(res5, "occupancy_5_online_LE.csv")
save_results(res5, "hmm_5_online_le.RData")
```
